title: Chai Price Time Travel
blurb: Guess what a cup of chai will cost in ten years, and see what rising prices do to money in a box.
t1.title: Chai through the years
t1.hook: A cup of chai cost {p0} when Asha's grandfather was young. Then it was {p1}, then {p2}, and now {p3}. Your mission: understand why.
t1.define: **Inflation** is the rise in prices over time. The same rupees buy less and less.
t1.analogy: Think of a chai stall's price board. Each time the owner rubs out the old price and writes a new one, your rupee shrinks a little.
q1.prompt: Chai went from {p0} to {p3} over the years. What is this rise in prices called?
q1.explain: A steady rise in prices over time is called inflation.
q2.prompt: When prices rise, what happens to what 100 rupees can buy?
q2.opt.d: It depends only on the bank
q2.explain: When prices rise, the same rupees buy less.
t2.title: Guess the price
t2.define: A model can estimate the future price by assuming prices rise at a steady rate. Real prices jump around, so treat the answer as a range, not a promise.
t2.formula: Future price = price today × (1 + inflation)^years. Example: a ₹50 meal with 4% inflation for 3 years costs 50 × 1.04 × 1.04 × 1.04, about ₹56.
t2.predict: What will one cup cost in {years} years, if prices keep rising about {infl} a year?
t2.reveal: Prices rising {infl} a year turn {price} into about {future}. This is an estimate, built on a made-up steady rate.
q3.prompt: Suppose prices rise {infMid} a year instead. What does a cup cost after {years} years? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: Multiply {price} by 1.05, {years} times. A calculator helps.
q3.explain: {price} grown at {infMid} a year for {years} years is about {midFuture}.
t3.title: Money in a box
t3.hook: Asha keeps {money} in a box at home. Not a rupee is ever taken out. Your mission: see what it can buy in the future.
t3.formula: Value in today's money = amount ÷ (1 + inflation)^years. Example: ₹2,000 after 3 years of 4% inflation is worth 2,000 ÷ 1.04 ÷ 1.04 ÷ 1.04, about ₹1,778.
t3.explore: Open the lab. Set the inflation to {infl} and slide the years to {years}. Watch the cups.
q4.prompt: In the lab, how many whole cups does {money} buy after {years} years of {infl} inflation? Type a number.
q4.hint: Read the cups for the later price in the lab.
q4.explain: A cup then costs about {future}. {money} buys {cupsThen} whole cups, instead of {cupsNow} today.
q5.prompt: In today's money, what is that {money} worth after {years} years of {infl} inflation? Type a number in rupees.
q5.explain: Prices rise, so the same {money} has the buying power of only about {realVal} of today's money.
q6.prompt: Asha's {money} sits in the box and never loses a rupee. Is it safe from inflation?
q6.opt.a: No. The rupees stay, but they buy less each year
q6.opt.b: Yes, the same rupees mean the same value
q6.opt.c: Yes, it grows by itself in the box
q6.fb.b: The number of rupees stays the same, but prices rise, so what they buy shrinks.
q6.hint: Compare the cups today with the cups later.
q6.explain: Money in a box keeps its rupees but loses buying power as prices rise.
t4.title: Real return
t4.define: Your **nominal return** is the percent your money grows. Your **real return** is what is left after inflation. It tells you if you can buy more, or less, than before.
t4.note: A simple way to estimate it: the growth rate minus the inflation rate. The exact way divides one plus growth by one plus inflation.
q7.prompt: A safe place pays {nominal} a year, and prices rise {infl}. About what is the real return? Type a percentage. Use a minus sign for a loss.
q7.hint: Compare the growth with the rise in prices. Which is bigger?
q7.explain: Money grows {nominal} but prices rise {infl}, so buying power changes by about {realRet} a year.
q8.prompt: A real return below zero means...
q8.opt.a: You can buy less than before, even if the number of rupees grew
q8.opt.b: You lost rupees from your account
q8.hint: Real return is about what your money can buy.
q8.explain: A negative real return means buying power shrank, even when the rupee amount went up.
